look.plainEnglish: The look is a short timer, not a frame loop. The trace starts at the camera, reaches about five meters so a doorway is in range, and ignores the player who is holding the camera.
look.whyGame: A frame loop traces while you stand still, and including the owner sticks the prompt to your own capsule.

expansions.title: The timer
expansions.detail: A tenth of a second is enough. The frame loop is not.

expansions.title: The distance
expansions.detail: Five meters reaches a door without scanning the map.

expansions.title: The owner
expansions.detail: Add the owner to the ignore list.

quiz.prompt: What schedules the foundation look?
choices: A check on every idle frame
quiz.why: A timer asks. A frame loop never stops.

quiz.prompt: The sample starts the look with a timer of 0.1 seconds, looping. What does that line avoid?
choices: A query on every idle frame
quiz.why: Standing still should not trace.

quiz.prompt: How far is this course's look?
choices: 50 centimeters, which stops at the barrel
quiz.why: Five meters reaches a door.

quiz.prompt: The trace includes the owner. What does the prompt stick to?
quiz.why: Ignore the player who is looking.

quiz.prompt: You move the look onto the frame loop so focus never feels late. What keeps being paid for?
choices: A physics query while the player stands still
A stack cap on the item
quiz.why: The timer already asks often enough.

quiz.prompt: The foundation look trace should ignore the player who is holding the camera.
quiz.why: The owner is ignored.

quiz.prompt: Where does the look start?
quiz.why: The player looks through the camera.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the foundation look, not the broken one?
choices: A looping timer that ignores the owner
A frame function that can hit the player
A widget click that hardcodes a distance
quiz.why: Timer, player ignored.

quiz.prompt: The trace is 50 centimeters. What doorway does the player fail to reach?
choices: One a step ahead, past the barrel
The owner's own capsule, correctly ignored
A slot the widget already drew
quiz.why: Five meters is the course distance.

quiz.prompt: What do you add so the owner is not a hit?
choices: The owner, on the trace's ignore list
A second trace from the feet
quiz.why: Ignore the player who is looking.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why is the tactical look a short timer from the camera, about five meters, that ignores the owner?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What keeps tracing while you stand still, and what prompt sticks to your capsule, if it is a frame loop that includes the owner?

carry.plainEnglish: The item data owns the stack size. The component decides whether another one fits. The widget only draws the slots that decision already made. The authority is who may add.
carry.whyGame: A hardcoded 99 in the click drifts from the next item, and a local add desyncs the other machines.

expansions.title: Max stack
expansions.detail: It lives on the item data, not in the click.

expansions.title: The widget
expansions.detail: It draws. It does not decide.

expansions.title: The add
expansions.detail: The authority adds. A client prediction is not the stock.

quiz.prompt: Where does the max stack live?
quiz.why: The data owns the number.

quiz.prompt: The click checks Count against Item->MaxStack. What does that line read?
choices: The cap the item data already named
A literal 99 typed in the handler
quiz.why: The component asks the data.

quiz.prompt: The stack is already at the data's cap. What should the add do?
quiz.why: Full means stop.

quiz.prompt: The widget click hardcodes 99. What drifts when the next item caps at 5?
choices: The item data, which updates itself
quiz.why: The number in the click is the bug.

quiz.prompt: What should the inventory widget do?
choices: Draw the slots the component already decided
quiz.why: The widget is a view.

quiz.prompt: An inventory add counts only when the authority accepts it.
quiz.why: The authority adds.

quiz.prompt: Who may add an item?
choices: Whoever clicked, keeping that add as the lasting stock
A check on every idle frame
quiz.why: A local add desyncs the others.

quiz.prompt: A client adds a magazine before the server answers. What do the other players still have?
quiz.why: Their machines never saw an authority add.

quiz.prompt: Which check is the stack rule in the right place?
choices: Count compared with the item's max stack
A frame loop that scans every item
A mesh pointer compared with null
quiz.why: Read the data.

quiz.prompt: The widget draws a sixth slot the component refused. What did the view invent?
choices: A slot the decision never made
The correct cap from the data
quiz.why: Draw what was decided. Do not decide.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does the item data own the stack size, while the component decides whether another one fits?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What drifts from the next item, and what desyncs the other machines, if the click hardcodes 99 or the add is only local?

wear.plainEnglish: Wear is a number. Replicate that number. When it arrives, OnRep plays the scuff. Leave the mesh where it is. The mesh is already on the weapon.
wear.whyGame: Replicating the mesh shares a pointer. The thing that changed is the wear value.

expansions.title: The property
expansions.detail: DOREPLIFETIME on Wear, not on the mesh.

expansions.title: The scuff
expansions.detail: OnRep plays it after the value arrives.

expansions.title: The mesh
expansions.detail: It stays on the weapon. It is not the replicated fact.

quiz.prompt: What should replicate when the gun wears?
choices: The whole weapon actor every frame
quiz.why: Clients need the number.

quiz.prompt: DOREPLIFETIME names Wear. What does that line share?
quiz.why: Wear is the property.

quiz.prompt: The new wear value arrives. What should run?
choices: A tick that wears the gun down again
A widget click that sets the cap
quiz.why: The notify is the local reaction.

quiz.prompt: OnRep also subtracts wear again. What does one scuff become?
choices: One scuff from the server number
quiz.why: The value already arrived. Play it.

quiz.prompt: You replicate the mesh pointer instead. What did the other machines receive?
choices: A pointer, not the number that changed
quiz.why: The mesh was already there.

quiz.prompt: The wear system should replicate the weapon mesh.
quiz.why: Leave the mesh where it is.

quiz.prompt: Which replication line is the right property?
choices: The wear value on the wear component
The weapon mesh on that component
quiz.why: Wear changed. The mesh did not.

quiz.prompt: A client sets wear locally so the scuff appears early. What corrects?
choices: The scuff, when the server value arrives
quiz.why: The local number was not the replicated one.

quiz.prompt: Why leave the mesh where it is?
choices: It is already on the weapon
The look trace owns the mesh
quiz.why: The mesh did not change. The number did.

quiz.prompt: Which function is the scuff, not a second subtract?
choices: OnRep of wear, playing the reaction
A frame loop that reduces wear again
A client write of the mesh pointer
quiz.why: Present the value. Do not change it again.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why do you replicate the wear number and play the scuff from OnRep, leaving the mesh on the weapon?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What pointer gets shared with every client if the mesh is replicated instead of the wear value?

connect.plainEnglish: Input asks. It calls try-interact, and the interaction component decides. Health and inventory change on the authority. The prompt listens for focus changing. It does not poll.
connect.whyGame: Input that traces itself hides the interaction component, and a prompt that polls on the frame loop stays awake after focus has already changed.

expansions.title: The key
expansions.detail: It calls try-interact. It does not apply damage.

expansions.title: The prompt
expansions.detail: Bind to focus changed. Do not read focus every frame.

expansions.title: The bar
expansions.detail: It shows health. The authority changes health.

quiz.prompt: What should the interact key call?
choices: Hurting the target straight from the key
A stack-cap write in the widget
quiz.why: Input is a request.

quiz.prompt: The key calls Try Interact and the interaction component traces. What did input correctly refuse to do?
quiz.why: Interaction decides.

quiz.prompt: How does the prompt hear that focus changed?
choices: It binds to the focus-changed event
It reads focus on the frame loop
quiz.why: The event fires when focus actually changes.

quiz.prompt: The prompt reads focus every frame. What stays awake after focus has moved on?
choices: Only the binding, which already fired
quiz.why: Polling hides the moment of the change.

quiz.prompt: Who is allowed to change health?
choices: Every client on the frame loop
quiz.why: The bar shows the number. It does not subtract it.

quiz.prompt: The health widget should subtract health.
quiz.why: UI listens.

quiz.prompt: Inventory changes on the same rule as health. Who writes the stack?
quiz.why: The view draws. The server decides.

quiz.prompt: Which binding is the prompt, not the poll?
choices: A frame function that copies the focused actor
A cast to every door class
quiz.why: Listen. Do not poll.

quiz.prompt: Input applies damage directly. What component was skipped?
choices: The wear notify, which should have damaged
The widget, which should have subtracted
The item data, which should have traced
quiz.why: The key asks. Something else decides.

quiz.prompt: Which order matches input, interaction, authority, and UI?
choices: Ask, decide, write the number, then listen
A poll that subtracts in the widget, traces every frame, and ignores the server
Sharing the weapon mesh, hardcoding 99, hitting the owner, then ticking
Damage from the key, focus from the constructor, wear from the widget
quiz.why: That is how the four systems connect.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does input call try-interact and let the interaction component decide, with health and inventory changing only on the authority?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What component disappears, and what prompt stays awake, if input traces by itself or the prompt polls every frame?
